candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; initiate appropriate referrals and collaborate with interprofessional resources to meet client needs
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — referral for diabetes self-management education and support
candidate.educational_objective: Refer clients with diabetes to DSMES for individualized education and support in self-care skills, problem-solving, goal setting, and sustainable health behaviors beginning at diagnosis and at other critical times of need.

options.A: A diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) service, where a trained diabetes care and education professional can provide individualized self-management education, goal setting, and problem-solving support.
options.B: A scheduling office whose role is limited to arranging follow-up appointments without providing diabetes self-management education.
options.C: A specialist whose primary role is to independently prescribe all diabetes medications in every state regardless of professional licensure or scope-of-practice law.
options.D: No referral is indicated because DSMES is intended only for clients who have already developed a diabetes complication.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care advise all people with diabetes to participate in DSMES. DSMES supports informed decision-making, self-care behaviors, problem-solving, active collaboration with the health care team, goal setting, and behavior-change strategies, and it should be provided at diagnosis and again at other critical times. B does not meet the client’s educational and behavioral needs. C makes an invalid universal scope-of-practice claim; prescribing authority depends on the professional’s license and applicable law, not the diabetes-education credential alone. D is incorrect because diagnosis itself is a recommended time for DSMES.
candidate.source_claim_supported: DSMES is a person-centered educational and behavioral-support intervention for people with diabetes and is recommended beginning at diagnosis; it helps build self-management skills, problem-solving, and sustainable behavior change.
candidate.source_document_title: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: DSMES Recommendations 5.1–5.5 and accompanying text — advise all people with diabetes to participate in DSMES; provide at diagnosis and other critical times; support informed decision-making, self-care behaviors, problem-solving, active collaboration, goal setting, and behavioral strategies
candidate.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
candidate.stem: A client newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes understands the medication prescription but says, “I don’t know how to fit glucose monitoring, meals, activity, and problem-solving into daily life.” Which referral would most directly address this need?
